title: Alexander: the return matters
hook: Did the expedition keep moving east until it ended?

knows: Events happen in places and at different times.

claims.text: 334 BCE: Crossing. The army crosses the Hellespont.
claims.source: https://www.metmuseum.org/essays/the-rise-of-macedonia-and-the-conquests-of-alexander-the-great — Hemingway and Hemingway, 2004, paragraphs on 334 BCE, Indus, return and division

claims.text: 330s BCE: Conquests. Campaigns take in Egypt and Persia.
claims.source: https://www.metmuseum.org/essays/the-rise-of-macedonia-and-the-conquests-of-alexander-the-great — Hemingway and Hemingway, 2004, paragraphs on 334 BCE, Indus, return and division

claims.text: Later: Eastern reach. The expedition reaches the Indus region.
claims.source: https://www.metmuseum.org/essays/the-rise-of-macedonia-and-the-conquests-of-alexander-the-great — Hemingway and Hemingway, 2004, paragraphs on 334 BCE, Indus, return and division

claims.text: 323 BCE: Return. The army turns back; Alexander dies at Babylon.
claims.source: https://www.metmuseum.org/essays/the-rise-of-macedonia-and-the-conquests-of-alexander-the-great — Hemingway and Hemingway, 2004, paragraphs on 334 BCE, Indus, return and division

claims.text: The map bends back west. The Macedonian army’s eastern reach did not become an endless advance: the soldiers insisted on returning. Alexander died at Babylon, and the conquests were divided among generals. Army decisions and succession mattered alongside the commander.
claims.source: https://www.metmuseum.org/essays/the-rise-of-macedonia-and-the-conquests-of-alexander-the-great — Hemingway and Hemingway, 2004, paragraphs on 334 BCE, Indus, return and division
